lesson.meaning: To use something up, eat or drink something, or to take a lot of time or energy.
examples: It's important to consume enough water throughout the day to stay healthy.
Our new project will consume a significant amount of the team's time and resources.
The old machinery tends to consume too much electricity, leading to higher bills.
Customers are increasingly consuming digital content, like e-books and online courses.
Please don't consume all the printer paper; we need some for the morning meeting.
lesson.memory_tip: Think of 'consuming' a big meal or 'consuming' a lot of data on your phone. It means you are taking it in or using it up!
